title: Introduce service-claim circuit breaker and KMS residency prober
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds operator-scoped circuit breaker to prevent unintended cross-region KMS usage, a residency prober for service claims, RBAC v2 policy mapper adjustments, and offline audit collector hardening. Controls are behind feature flags and rollout is canaryed by tenant.
description: Motivation: Several internal incidents revealed that operator-scoped service claims could accidentally exercise KMS keys in non-resident regions when fallback heuristics engaged. This PR adds a defensive circuit breaker at the service-claim layer that blocks KMS operations when residency constraints fail a liveness/prober check, plus a self-contained residency prober that continuously verifies service-to-region affinity. The change also tightens RBAC v2 mapping so operator-scoped grants are rejected if the claim does not match residency assertions, and hardens the offline audit collector to include provenance tags and scrubbed context for any breaker-triggered events. Implementation overview: 1) New package services/kms/circuit_breaker.go implements a token bucket backed circuit breaker with exponential backoff and a short-term denylist keyed by (service, tenant, attempted_kms_region). The breaker exposes metrics: kms.breaker.allowed, kms.breaker.denied, kms.breaker.backoff_seconds. 2) services/kms/residency_prober.go implements a residency prober that runs a lightweight key-assertion handshake against configured KMS endpoints and caches results with TTL and jitter. Prober results are surfaced to the breaker via a compact status struct. 3) RBAC v2 policy mapping adjusted in rbac/policy/mapper.go to evaluate residency claims (attribute: residency.region) during decision time; missing residency attributes cause a soft-deny path which the breaker can escalate to a hard block when the feature flag is enabled. 4) audit/offline_collector.go extended to include event provenance (prober_result, breaker_reason) and to redact tenant PII for any breaker-related audit forwards. 5) Helm values and operator docs updated to include feature flags rbac.v2.residency_enforce and kms.breaker.enabled and rollout knobs per-tenant. 6) New unit and integration tests covering prober race conditions, breaker backoff behavior, and RBAC attribute evaluation. Migration: tenants with custom KMS mappings must add residency.region claim to service bindings or opt-out by annotation until migration is complete.

Known risks and mitigations: Risk: false-positive breaker activations causing client errors. Mitigation: staged rollout with log_only mode and alerting, 48h canary window, quick revert flag kms.breaker.enabled=false.
Risk: increased latency from prober calls. Mitigation: prober uses cached status with TTL and jitter, local cache on each host, and prober calls are async where possible.

Risk: RBAC policy eval path change could affect non-residency tenants. Mitigation: default policy path still allows access unless residency_enforce is turned on; documented opt-out annotation for legacy tenants.
Observability and runbook pointers: Metrics: kms.breaker.denied, kms.breaker.allowed, kms.breaker.backoff_seconds, rbac.residency_checks.total, audit.breaker_events.count
Dashboards: Security / KMS Residency -> added panel for breaker spikes
Runbook: docs/runbooks/kms-residency-rollout.md contains rollback steps, metrics to watch, and how to disable per-tenant via annotation
